text: On Locke's empiricist account, our idea of duration is derived from:
choices: A pure a priori intuition that precedes and conditions all experience
An absolute time that God constitutes through his infinite duration and omnipresence
The intuitive grasp of things in their necessity, sub specie aeternitatis
Reflection on the succession of ideas as they come and go in our own minds
explanation: Locke grounds the idea of duration in reflection on the constant succession of ideas passing through the mind (Essay II.14.3) — an inner, empirical source, not any external independent framework. Choice 0 is Kant's a priori intuition, choice 1 is the Newtonian God-constituted absolute time, and choice 2 is Spinoza's eternity; these are precisely the non-empiricist alternatives that Locke's derivation-from-experience rejects.
